CNP.thesis_one_line: Houston's regulated power-delivery utility, building toward huge new electricity demand at a lower price than its own long-term growth promise implies.
kill_criteria: Consolidated net debt/EBITDA rises above 6.5x for two consecutive quarters (vs. ~5.5x now).
FFO/debt falls below 11% (vs. ~13% now) on a trailing-twelve-month basis, per company or rating-agency-reported figures.
Full-year non-GAAP EPS guidance is cut from the current $1.89-$1.91 range (any downward revision, not just a miss).
The 4.25% convertible notes due 2026 are confirmed to have required a distressed or unfavourable refinancing (materially above the ~2.9% coupon on the 2029 tranche priced in Feb 2026).
ERCOT Batch Zero 'qualified' large-load capacity (currently ~14 GW) falls by more than 30% in a subsequent quarterly update, signalling the demand pipeline is not converting.
key_adverse_facts: Consolidated FFO/debt ~13.0-13.4% and net debt/EBITDA ~5.5x are elevated for a T&D utility and have risen, not fallen, alongside the accelerating capital plan (secondary-source aggregation, cross-check only).
A $1.0bn 4.25% convertible note matured/converted 15 Aug 2026; this diligence window could not confirm how it was settled (open data gap).
FCF has been structurally and materially negative for two years running (e.g., -$1,677m 9-month 2025) as capex outruns operating cash flow.
data_conflicts: b1_live_scores.csv's high fcfp (FCF-yield) percentile appears to be computed pre-capex-netting; on an actual FCF basis (OCF minus capex) CNP is deeply cash-flow-negative, so the model's 'value/cheap' signal partly reflects a metric-definition artefact for a heavy-capex utility, not cash-rich cheapness.
CNP.confidence_in_thesis: medium (guidance and rate-base growth are well-documented; leverage direction and the convertible-note settlement are open items that could change the picture)

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 systematic valuation row exists for CNP, so v1_verdict is null; the dossier's own simplified dividend/earnings-growth reverse model implies ~5.9%/yr (DV10 2026-10-09: dividend input corrected to $0.96; ~7.6%/yr at a 10.2% discount rate, so the gap to the 7-9% target is rate-sensitive) long-run growth priced in, below management's guided 7-9%/yr long-term EPS growth range, i.e. the stock appears to price in less growth than the company is guiding to.

CNP.scenario_basis: Starting point: $1.90 2026 non-GAAP EPS guidance midpoint at a 19.4x NTM P/E ($36.84 close); base case assumes the guided 7-9% EPS growth persists with a stable ~19-20x multiple and a modest dividend yield; bear assumes a leverage-driven credit event compresses the multiple to ~15x with growth stalling near 3-4%; bull assumes the ERCOT large-load pipeline converts faster than guided, EPS growth runs at the high end of 9%, and the multiple re-rates toward 21-22x.

D.thesis_one_line: Virginia's data-center-powering utility is being acquired by NextEra Energy; the stock now trades on deal-completion odds, not on its own growth story.
kill_criteria: Any regulator (Virginia SCC, North Carolina, South Carolina, FERC, or NRC) formally denies or imposes conditions materially impairing deal economics.
The merger agreement is terminated by either party, or the expected close date is pushed beyond 2028 (vs. 'late 2027' guided now).
The arb spread (deal value implied by NEE's price and the 0.8138 exchange ratio, minus D's price) widens beyond 8% annualised, signalling the market has repriced completion risk upward.
CVOW's cost estimate rises by a further $500m or more from the current $11.7bn, or the completion date slips beyond mid-2028.
Dominion's consolidated long-term debt grows more than 10% in a single year again (matching or exceeding the 2024-to-2025 pace of ~18%) without a matching rating-agency reaffirmation.
key_adverse_facts: A signed, pending all-stock-plus-cash merger with NextEra Energy (15 May 2026; 0.8138 NEE shares + ~$360m aggregate cash) was not surfaced by the Q15 triage at all; b1_live_scores.csv's own exclude_pending_deal flag is already True for D.
CVOW (Coastal Virginia Offshore Wind) cost has risen twice in the history reviewed, now to ~$11.7bn, with 19% of construction remaining and turbine-installation risk explicitly cited by management.
Consolidated long-term debt rose ~18% in one year (2024-12-31 to 2025-12-31: $39,320m to $46,332m), the largest single-year jump in the multi-year series reviewed.
data_conflicts: The Q15 triage's one-line thesis and reason describe D as a standalone growth-utility story ('finishing the largest US offshore wind project'); it omits the pending NextEra merger entirely, which this dossier treats as the dominant fact for D's valuation and eligibility.
D.horizon: 14-18 months (tied to expected merger close, 'late 2027' per NextEra management)
D.confidence_in_thesis: medium (merger terms and regulatory-filing dates are documented in SEC filings; the ultimate closing timeline, NEE's price path, and CVOW's final cost are all open)

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: DV12: deal-arb basis unchanged (about 2.7% spread to ~$62.31 implied value, roughly 2.3%/yr to a 2H-2027 close). Standalone fallback restated: actual dividend $2.67 (75% payout of $3.57) at r 8.5% implies 3.9% perpetual growth (earlier 5.85% used a wrong 45% payout), below the 5-7% historical guided EPS growth, so standalone implied_vs_base is below; headline implied_vs_base kept in_line because the deal spread governs. Dominion shareholders approved the merger on 3 Sep 2026.

D.scenario_basis: Starting point: $60.68 close vs. ~$62.31 implied deal value (0.8138 x NEE's $76.08 close plus ~$0.41/share cash); base case assumes the deal closes roughly on the 'late 2027' schedule, delivering the thin arb spread annualised over the sleeve's 3-year window plus D's ~4-5% dividend yield while pending; bear assumes a regulatory denial or termination, D reverts toward a standalone value near $50-55 (multiple compression on rising leverage and CVOW risk) before recovering some; bull assumes an accelerated, on-terms close plus NEE share-price appreciation between now and closing (D holders receive NEE stock).

EW.thesis_one_line: Structural-heart device leader growing TAVR and its faster mitral/tricuspid franchise, but priced for more 10-year growth than the evidence supports.
kill_criteria: TAVR constant-currency sales growth falls below 7%/yr for two consecutive quarters (below even the low end of the pre-raise guidance range).
TMTT sales growth decelerates below 25%/yr year-over-year for two consecutive quarters (roughly half its current ~45% pace).
Adjusted EPS guidance is cut from the current $2.95-$3.05 range (any downward revision).
FCF/net-income conversion falls back below 70% on a trailing-two-quarter basis (vs. ~91% now).
A major TAVR or TMTT clinical trial results in a materially adverse label change or safety signal for an Edwards device.
key_adverse_facts: Reverse DCF implies ~12.5%/yr 10-year FCF growth priced into the $86.29 close, above the analyst's evidence-based base case of ~9-10%/yr.
ROE (~9% per b1 factor data) is modest for a ~28.8x NTM P/E.

Q2 2026 GAAP net income fell ~27% y/y ($241.9m vs. $333.2m) even as adjusted EPS grew, driven partly by a California R&D tax-credit change; Medtronic's Evolut, Abbott's Navitor (seeking label expansion), and Boston Scientific's planned Acurate Neo2 re-entry are all named, active TAVR competitive threats.
EW.confidence_in_thesis: high (guidance quotes, XBRL financials and the competitive landscape are all well-documented and mutually consistent)

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 systematic valuation row exists for EW, so v1_verdict is null; the dossier's own reverse FCF-DCF (WACC 8%, terminal growth 3%) implies ~12.5%/yr 10-year FCF growth priced into the $86.29 close, above a ~9-10%/yr evidence-based base case blending TAVR's guided 8-9% and TMTT's faster but smaller-base growth, so the stock is priced above what the base case supports.

EW.scenario_basis: Starting point: FCF/share ~$1.96 (H1 2026 annualised) at $86.29 (~44x FCF); base case assumes ~9-10%/yr FCF growth with the multiple compressing modestly toward a more normal ~35-38x as growth normalises post the TMTT ramp; bear assumes TAVR competitive share loss (Boston Scientific re-entry, Abbott label expansion) drags growth to mid-single digits with multiple compression to ~28-30x; bull assumes TMTT continues compounding near 40%+ and TAVR holds 8-9%, supporting the current premium multiple.
